page: Amazon Web Services r7a.4xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine delivered on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. It is driven by a 16-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor configured with a single thread per physical core, operating at clock frequencies reaching 3.7 GHz. Cache allocation includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The CPU features broad hardware extension support, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI instructions.

Memory provisioning stands at 128 GB of DDR5 running at 5 GHz, establishing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation ratio tailored for memory-heavy computing. The server contains no local NVMe storage drives, directing all disk I/O operations through remote network block storage. Networking capability includes a dedicated 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without included public IPv4 addresses, and the configuration contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations showcase top-quartile single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core figures ranking in the upper 25% of tested systems. The platform also registered top-tier token generation speeds in small-parameter language model processing. Multi-core operations, compiler tasks, and full-scale PassMark compute scores sit consistently within mid-tier operational bounds. Memory access tests delivered steady uncached block bandwidth of 75.99 GB/sec read and 54.91 GB/sec write.

The r7a.4xlarge balances high memory bandwidth and dedicated AMD core execution, though workloads requiring heavy local disk I/O will face latency overhead due to reliance on external storage volumes. Given the 128 GB DDR5 footprint and robust single-core compute performance, this server is suitable for running in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational database systems, ETL processing, and memory-constrained data science jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and equipped with 16 dedicated physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at up to 3.7 GHz. Featuring an x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 vector extensions, this instance is paired with 128 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per core memory profile. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps and does not include bundled local instance storage, relying entirely on network-attached volumes for data persistence. In synthetic and practical benchmarks, the r7a.4xlarge demonstrates strong single-core CPU execution, exceptional text processing, and top-tier token throughput during small language model inference, alongside stable mid-range multi-core compute capability. With its substantial memory density and solid single-thread performance, this server offers a balanced profile for in-memory databases, key-value stores like Redis, and memory-bound analytics pipelines.
